description: UUID_STRING in both forms. The two-argument UUID_STRING(namespace, name) is an RFC 4122 version-5 (SHA-1) named UUID and is BIT-EXACT: the pair asserted here is the documented Snowflake example. It is deterministic, a numeric name is used as its text, and neither argument is null-propagating - a NULL or malformed NAMESPACE is an error while a NULL NAME hashes as the empty string and still yields a UUID (live-measured; the class asserted NULL for both until it was moved onto the shared test base and actually ran live). The no-argument form is random, matches the RFC layout and differs on every evaluation. UUID_STRING may not appear in a VALUES clause - live-measured, and by NAME rather than by determinism, since the exact two-argument form is refused there too while CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() passes - so INSERT ... SELECT is the supported route. Converted 1:1 from functions/UuidStringTest (now retired); Java-side Pattern.matches became REGEXP_LIKE and the two-query uniqueness comparison became COUNT(DISTINCT ...) over a GENERATOR scan.

steps.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE sample_generate_uuid (
  id UUID DEFAULT UUID_STRING() NOT NULL,
  sample_column VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE with_uuid (id UUID, name VARCHAR)
